title: Prospective model-fallback catalog: latency-cost probe & procurement triggers
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, operational catalog that maps candidate open and partner model variants to prescriptive fallback strategies (region, quantization, cheaper variant, cached-prefix). The catalog will include measured latency distributions, token-cost delta, quality delta (sampled evals), and procurement/provisioning triggers that the SRE/Provisioning team can consume.

Why now: Sales and SRE have seen three mid-market incidents in the last 60 days where hosted model availability degraded regionally and the application-level fallbacks either increased latency >2x or surfaced quality regressions. We need an explicitly tested fallback matrix so customer-facing apps can route to a predictable alternative without manual operator intervention.

Scope and deliverables (MVP):
- A canonical spreadsheet (and exported JSON) of ~20 prioritized model variants (open & partner) with the following columns: region tested, quantization level, median p50/p95 latency at typical batch sizes, tokens/sec throughput, per-token cost estimate, measured quality delta against our vertical prompt set, and suggested fallback policy entry (e.g., quantized-8bit, smaller-context variant, cached-prefix).
- A synthesis doc (Confluence) summarizing trade-offs for three common fallbacks: quantization, smaller-seq-length variant, and tiered routing. Include recommended SLO guardrails and rollout checklist.
- 6 field probes run against our synthetic workloads and two customer anonymized workloads; results pushed to runtime dashboard + a short interpretive note for sales and SRE.
- A pre-configured alert rule and procurement trigger: when region availability drops below X% for Y minutes, autoprovide to an approved reserved pool or escalate with explicit model fallback path.

Approach:
1) Competitive scan: include 8 external model variants (open-source forks + partner-stable flavors) and 12 internal candidate variants. Extract initial latency/cost estimates from published benchmarks, then run a controlled lab harness on Dedicated staging.
2) Field probes: run 1-hour rolling probes per region (NA/EU/APAC) capturing p50/p95 latency under typical prompt length distributions. Measure quality using a 50-item vertical eval prompt set (paired human review on edge cases).
3) Synthesis: combine telemetry, qualitative notes, and procurement-level economics into a single decision canvas per variant with a recommended fallback maturity (experimental / approved / enterprise-ready).

Artifacts and links: 
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Prospective+Fallback+Catalog
- Spreadsheet (single source): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/driveid/fallback-catalog-2026-03.csv
- Lab harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probe-harness/pull/189
- Runtime dashboard (staging): https://dash.redwood.internal/runtime/fallback-probes

Rollout & handoff: deliverable will be reviewed with SRE (ops-runbook review) and Growth/Sales (customer-facing guidance). Handoff checklist includes: approved fallback variants list, alert thresholds JSON, and a small example router policy (yaml) for the runtime team to import into canary routing configs.
